'''Guido Caldarelli''' (born in 1967) is an Italian [[physicist]] (statistical physics) and [[Professor#Other positions|full professor]] in Theoretical Physics at [[Ca' Foscari University of Venice]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.unive.it/data/persone/24068586|title=Ricerca persone}}</ref> From 2024 he is Director of the Institute of Complex Systems of the [[National Research Council of Italy]]

==Biography==
Caldarelli received his Ph.D. from [[SISSA]], after which he was a postdoc in the Department of Physics and School of Biology,  [[University of Manchester]]. He then worked at the [[Theory of Condensed Matter]] Group, [[University of Cambridge]], where he worked with [[Robin Ball]]. He returned to Italy as a lecturer at the National Institute for Condensed Matter (INFM)  and later as Primo Ricercatore in the Institute of Complex Systems of the [[National Research Council of Italy]]. During this period, he was also the coordinator of the Networks subproject, part of the Complexity Project, for the [[Fermi Centre]]. From 2012 to 2020, he was a professor at [[IMT School for Advanced Studies Lucca]]. He also spent some terms at [[University of Fribourg]] (Switzerland) and across 2003–2004, he has been visiting professor at [[École Normale Supérieure]] in Paris.

In CCS2018 (The Conference of Complex Systems Society), he was elected President of the Complex Systems Society for the mandate 2018–2021.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://cssociety.org/about/executive-committee|title=CSS Executive Committee}}</ref>

From July 1, 2024, he is the Director of the Institute of Complex Systems of [[National Research Council (Italy)]].

==Research==
The activity of Caldarelli is mainly focused on [[scale-free networks]], [[complex network]]s in theoretical models and in their application to [[financial networks]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=RZid9X8AAAAJ&hl=it&oi=ao|title=Guido Caldarelli}}</ref> He has been coordinator of the European project COSIN, one of the first international activities based on the study of complex networks as well as coordinator of the European project FOC on the study of financial networks and the project MULTIPLEX on Multi-level Complex Networks. All this activity contributed to the creation of network science community in the early stage of this discipline.

He has published numerous papers in physics and interdisciplinary journals, including Physical Review Letters and Nature. His work on beauty and the [[stable marriage problem]] has been reported in the press.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/science/nature/992304.stm|title = BBC News &#124; SCI/TECH &#124; Beautiful people 'ruin' lives}}</ref> He is also known for his research activity on systemic risk in networks of financial institutions.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Battiston |first1=Stefano |last2=Caldarelli |first2=Guido |last3=May |first3=Robert M. |last4=Roukny |first4=Tarik |last5=Stiglitz |first5=Joseph E. |date=2016-09-06 |title=The price of complexity in financial networks |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences |language=en |volume=113 |issue=36 |pages=10031–10036 |doi=10.1073/pnas.1521573113 |issn=0027-8424 |pmc=5018742 |pmid=27555583|bibcode=2016PNAS..11310031B |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Battiston |first1=Stefano |last2=Caldarelli |first2=Guido |last3=Georg |first3=Co-Pierre |last4=May |first4=Robert |last5=Stiglitz |first5=Joseph |date=March 2013 |title=Complex derivatives |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/nphys2575 |journal=Nature Physics |language=en |volume=9 |issue=3 |pages=123–125 |doi=10.1038/nphys2575 |bibcode=2013NatPh...9..123B |s2cid=15570077 |issn=1745-2481|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

==Honours==
*2019, Caldarelli has been awarded with the Network Society Fellowship <ref>{{Cite web|url=https://netscisociety.net/award-prizes/society-fellows|title=NetSci – the Network Science Society}}</ref> 
*2020, with the Network Society Service Award.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://netscisociety.net/award-prizes/service-award|title = NetSci – the Network Science Society}}</ref> 
*2020, he has been elected Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]].,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=C&year=2020&unit_id=&institution=|title=APS Fellow Archive}}</ref> 
*2020, he has been elected Member of the [[Academia Europaea]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Caldarelli_Guido|title = Academy of Europe: Caldarelli Guido}}</ref>
* 2023, he has been awarded the Service Award from the [[Complex Systems Society]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://cssociety.org/community/awards/service-award|title = CCS Service Awards}}</ref>
* 2025, he has been awarded the Senior Scientific Award from the [[Complex Systems Society]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://cssociety.org/community/awards/senior-scientific-award|title = CCS Senior Scientific Awards}}</ref>

==Books==
Caldarelli is the author of ''Scale-free networks'' a textbook for graduate students published by [[Oxford University Press]].<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://global.oup.com/academic/product/scale-free-networks-9780199211517?cc=it&lang=en&|isbn = 978-0-19-921151-7|title = Scale-Free Networks: Complex Webs in Nature and Technology|series = Oxford Finance Series|date = 3 May 2007|publisher = Oxford University Press}}</ref> He also edited with [[World Scientific Press]] and [[Alessandro Vespignani]] another book ''Large Scale Structure and Dynamics of Complex Networks''<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://www.worldscientific.com/worldscibooks/10.1142/6455|doi = 10.1142/6455|title = Large Scale Structure and Dynamics of Complex Networks|series = Complex Systems and Interdisciplinary Science|year = 2007|volume = 2|isbn = 978-981-270-664-5|last1 = Caldarelli|first1 = Guido|last2 = Vespignani|first2 = Alessandro}}</ref> on the activity of COSIN project.
In 2012, he published together with the colleague and journalist Michele Catanzaro the book ''Networks: A Very Short Introduction'' by Oxford University Press.<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://global.oup.com/academic/product/networks-a-very-short-introduction-9780199588077?cc=it&lang=en&|isbn = 978-0-19-958807-7|title = Networks: A Very Short Introduction|series = Very Short Introductions|date = 25 October 2012|publisher = Oxford University Press}}</ref> In 2016, he published with Alessandro Chessa the book  ''Data Science and Complex Networks'' by the same publisher.<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://global.oup.com/academic/product/data-science-and-complex-networks-9780199639601?q=caldarelli&lang=en&cc=it|isbn=978-0-19-963960-1|title=Data Science and Complex Networks: Real Case Studies with Python|date=15 September 2016|publisher=Oxford University Press}}</ref> In 2018 he edited together with Stefano Battiston and Antonios Garas the book ''Multiplex and Multilevel Networks'' again by Oxford University Press.<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://global.oup.com/academic/product/multiplex-and-multilevel-networks-9780198809456?q=caldarelli&lang=en&cc=it|isbn=978-0-19-880945-6|title=Multiplex and Multilevel Networks|date=7 November 2018|publisher=Oxford University Press}}</ref> He also coedited the book Networks in Cell Biology by [[Cambridge University Press]].<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/networks-in-cell-biology/30BDF60A4D3B80677B0B031CDB7B1E36|doi = 10.1017/CBO9780511845086|title = Networks in Cell Biology|year = 2010|publisher = Cambridge University Press|isbn = 9780511845086|editor1-last = Buchanan|editor1-first = Mark|editor2-first = Guido|editor2-last = Caldarelli|editor3-first = Paolo|editor3-last = De Los Rios|editor4-first = Francesco|editor4-last = Rao|editor5-first = Michele|editor5-last = Vendruscolo}}</ref>
